thread:
Oncall SRE: Pager: high error rate on customer Lighthouse Inc PrivateLink endpoint in eu-central-1 az2 — elevated 502/504 timeouts and TCP resets. Seeing ~30% request failures from that endpoint since 09:12 UTC. Incident Bot: incident INC-20260311-887 created and paged oncall.

Incident Bot: AUTO: linked runbook private-connectivity/bgp-flap (runbook id: pb-41).

Alyssa (netops): I see the customer path is flapping between two transit peers. BGP shows AS path teardown/shorter-path oscillation. Looks like a prepended route being withdrawn then re-advertised every ~30s.

Oncall SRE: Can you paste the BGP snippet? Also is secondary path healthy?

Alyssa (netops): Pasting filtered output: 
```
BGP State for prefix 10.182.0.0/22
* 203.0.113.12 from 198.51.100.2 (local AS 64512)
  AS_PATH: 64512 65100 65120
  NEXT_HOP: 198.51.100.2
  LAST_UPDATE: 2026-03-11 09:11:55
  Attributes: MED 0, LocalPref 100, community 64512:100
  — flapping: withdrawn 09:11:57, advertised 09:12:29, withdrawn 09:13:01
```

Ram (eng-runtime): We're seeing application-level retries amplify the effect. Traffic pools are getting uneven distribution because the endpoint is being intermittently blackholed. Is this only for eu-central-1 az2 or broader?

Lighthouse NOC: Confirming only eu-central-1 az2 PrivateLink target shows packet loss, healthcheck failing to 10.182.3.7. Other AZs okay.

Oncall SRE: Looks like the cloud-provider edge is oscillating the best path to the customer's edge (maybe BFD session resets). Alyssa, can you check BFD sessions and any interface errors on the transits?

Alyssa (netops): Running quick checks: 
```
# show bfd sessions | include 198.51.100.2
198.51.100.2 - state: up, uptime 00:03:12, last_update: 09:11:54
# show interface transit1 counters | include err|drop
transit1: input-errors 0, output-errors 0, drops 2 (workload level)
```
No clear local interface errors. BFD uptime is short — correlates with the withdraws. I suspect remote side flapping.

Jordan (CS): I'll message the Lighthouse NOC and tell them we're investigating and asking them to check their edge sessions. Jordan -> Lighthouse NOC: can you confirm if you pushed any config changes around 09:10 UTC?

Lighthouse NOC: No config pushed. We saw IPv4 route regen on our routers at ~09:11. We opened a ticket with our provider now.

Oncall SRE: Mitigation options: 1) Pin customer traffic to the secondary interconnect (route-policy override) for the affected AZ for a short window 2) Apply ephemeral longer flap dampening on transit to avoid rapid withdraw/advertise 3) Coordinate with customer/provider to fix upstream BGP instability.

Ram (eng-runtime): For immediate customer impact reduction, we can change the route-map for that prefix to prefer the non-flapping path (prefer next-hop 198.51.100.50) for eu-central az2. That requires a quick config push to edge-rt-euc1. I'll prepare the commands.

Alyssa (netops): Confirmed, pushing route preference will preserve connectivity while we troubleshoot. Expect ~45s for BGP to reconverge after policy commit.

Oncall SRE: Please include the exact changes in the incident log and request approval from netops lead if necessary. Tagging Ram and Alyssa for rollout.

Ram (eng-runtime): Plan: 
1) Apply route-map 'prefer-secondary-10.182/22' on edge-rt-euc1 outbound to set localpref 200 for next-hop 198.51.100.50
2) Monitor error rate and healthchecks for 10 minutes
3) If stable, coordinate with Lighthouse NOC to drain/repair their flapping session then revert policy.

Alyssa (netops): Command snippet for commit (dry-run validated): 
```
route-map prefer-secondary-10.182 permit 10
 set local-preference 200
neighbor 198.51.100.50 route-map prefer-secondary-10.182 out
commit confirmed 2m
```

Oncall SRE: Proceed when ready. Ram, roll in 30s. Jordan, send customer a heads-up that we may reroute traffic briefly.

Jordan (CS): Messaging now: "We're planning a short reroute for your eu-central-1 az2 traffic to reduce failed requests. Expect a brief reconverge window <90s. We'll confirm when stable."

Ram (eng-runtime): Pushing now. 

Incident Bot: change-log: route-policy apply edge-rt-euc1 by Ram (eng-runtime) @ 09:17:05 UTC.

Ram (eng-runtime): Done. Observability: error-rate dropped from 30% to 3% in ~60s. Healthchecks passing for PrivateLink target.

Alyssa (netops): BFD sessions still jittery on the primary 198.51.100.2 peer; we've opened a ticket with transit provider and asked for packet captures.

Lighthouse NOC: Confirming connectivity restored for az2, client reports lower latency and fewer 5xx. We'll keep our provider ticket open and follow up.

Oncall SRE: Impact assessment: Customer Lighthouse Inc — partial outage confined to eu-central-1 az2 PrivateLink target for ~09:12–09:17 UTC; mitigation by traffic preference began 09:17; observable error-rate reduced by ~90%. No data loss reported. Action items: 
- Netops to keep provider ticket open and share pcap when available (Alyssa).
- Ram to prepare revert runbook once upstream stable, include rollback test.
- Jordan to send customer summary and ETA for full remediation.

Jordan (CS): Sending post-incident summary now. Will include next steps and offer a conference bridge if Lighthouse wants deeper debug.

Alyssa (netops): Posting provider ticket ref: TP-66218 and attaching pcap. Provider acknowledges asymmetric flap, investigating.

Oncall SRE: Handoff inbound — my shift ends in 12m. Handoff notes: mitigation applied (route pref), monitoring stable, provider ticket open, contact points: Alyssa (netops) and Ram (eng-runtime). Next oncall please monitor for any reversion.

Incident Bot: escalation: paging next oncall (Oncall SRE 2) at 09:29 UTC as part of handoff.

Oncall SRE: Closing active paging. I'll add final timeline and set incident state to monitoring.

Lighthouse NOC: Thanks for the quick mitigation. We will follow up once our provider confirms root cause.

Ram (eng-runtime): I'll build the revert plan and schedule a controlled revert window with netops and the customer once provider confirms stability.

Oncall SRE: End of thread — summary saved to incident INC-20260311-887.
